refinement.detail: Searched, and the candidate was rejected on measurement. HP-05 adds no TLA+ construct, so there is no representation to refine; the refinement question available to this ticket is whether the `content:` declaration could be DERIVED instead of written, which would remove the one thing a project author still supplies. Three routes were considered and all three fail on this fixture. (1) Compare the durable artifact against the modeled state field the port writes: the model's COMMIT element is << "COMMIT", holder[r], amt[r] >> and carries no running total, so the comparison is blind to M04 by construction -- which is exactly why M04 survived both of HP-03's corpora. (2) Auto-correspond payload fields to after-state variables by NAME: the fixture's payload fields are `kind`, `tenant`, `amount`, `total` and the model's variables are `available`, `committed`, `closed`, `live`, `holder`, `amt`, `ledger`; not one name matches, and `total` refines `committed[tenant]`, which no naming rule recovers. (3) Infer the refinement from the implementation's line format: that is reading the code under test to build the oracle for the code under test, and it agrees with itself by construction (MF-028 lost a spike to exactly that shape). So the sentence stays authored. What HP-05 removed is the PROVIDER around it, which was the part every author wrote from scratch and the part the measured failure was in.

summary: Content assertion is the default: codegen generates and binds the content-asserting effect provider, every mapping states its oracles unprompted, and M04 moves from surviving every corpus to dying under the default mapping (durable_content 1 of 2 -> 2 of 2). The generator is still worse than the suite, now by one mutant instead of two.

assertions: A scaffolded project's providers assert content by default.
Every run states which mapping produced its numbers, unprompted.
A run under a mapping with no durable-write oracle says so in its output, not only in documentation.
acceptance.close_note: THE HEADLINE, AND IT IS ONE CELL: M04 moved from surviving every corpus instrument in every previous round to DYING under the default mapping. durable_content 1 of 2 -> 2 of 2. Same corpus, same adapter, same seam, same mutants; the only difference between the columns is one line of TOML naming a provider. Assertion 1 MET, with the boundary stated. Codegen now GENERATES the content-asserting provider for every manifest port with role: effect and BINDS it in case_adapters.toml for any effect port that has none -- additive only, so a table somebody wrote is never rewritten. A real project scaffolded from scratch, given one port declaration and nothing else, ends up asserting durable content with nobody writing a line of provider code (results/scaffolded-project.txt, run end to end). What is NOT met is the moment before the declaration exists: `scaffold project` still ships a `raise NotImplementedError` provider stub and a commented-out binding, and `scaffold_spec.py` / `onboard_program_model.py` are in no ticket's conflict keys and not in HP-05's edit permission. FILED as HP-05-DF-01. Assertions 2 and 3 MET on the paths this ticket owns, with the gap named rather than papered over. Codegen prints a full mapping audit unprompted on every invocation, and each generated provider announces its own binding on stdout the first time it binds. Four situations produce the SAME closing sentence -- silent provider bound, content-asserting provider with no `content:` block, role: effect port bound to nothing, and a boundary declared under `effects:` that no provider can reach (which is exactly how HP-01's own fixture declares LedgerAppendPort): "Nothing compares what crossed this port against the model, so kills counted under this mapping are a FLOOR, not a total, and a green run over-reads." All four captured verbatim in results/mapping-announcement.txt. THE GAP: the shipped runner never prints the mapping it loaded and does not pass it to the provider, so the announcement recovers the name from TLA_SPEC_DEV_MAPPING or from --mapping on the command line and says `<unnamed mapping>` when it cannot. run_generated_case_adapters.py is HP-04's conflict key. FILED as HP-05-DF-02. THREE THINGS THAT ARE UNFLATTERING, recorded here rather than only in the evidence. (1) M05 WAS ALREADY DYING. The ticket objective and the dispatch brief both say the two durable-side mutants survive both corpora. True of M04, FALSE of M05: HP-03's own committed kill table records M05 as KILLED by corpus-whole, and this run reproduces that under all three mappings. The model's CLOSE element is << "CLOSE", t, committed[t] >>, so its third slot IS the total and the ordinary projected-state comparison already sees a zeroed one; only the COMMIT element drops its total. ONE mutant moved, not two. (2) THE 30% FIGURE DOES NOT REPRODUCE AS A PROPORTION. On the blind agent's 16-mutant catalogue the mapping was worth 3 of 10 kills; here it is worth 1 of 6 under the checking mapping and 1 of 10 overall. The DIRECTION has now replicated three times on three fixtures. The MAGNITUDE is fixture-dependent and 30% must not be quoted as a property of the mechanism. (3) THE GENERATOR IS STILL WORSE THAN THE SUITE. Suite 10 of 10. Whole-view corpus under the checking mapping 6 of 10. Whole-view (checking) + HP-03's negative corpus 9 of 10, up from 8 of 10 -- the gap narrows from two mutants to one. The survivor is M07, the catalogue's declared POSITIVE CONTROL, which is supposed to die on every instrument and does not because it is seeded inside reserve() and Reserve contributes zero executable cases. While that control is red the wrong_value row is not citeable as a clean kill measurement. THE REPRODUCTION CONTROL, without which none of the above is readable. This instrument installs a seam the reference implementation does not have (the durable append goes through the port AND to the file), so a third column runs with no provider bound at all. It reproduces HP-03's committed `corpus-whole` column in all ten rows, so the map-checking column is a mapping effect and nothing else. Two full runs of the whole table were identical including failing executions. PER ARM: NOT MEASURABLE AT HP-05, for the reason HP-03 recorded -- the arms are implementations the A/B produces at HP-06 and neither has code yet. Every number is on the fixture's reference implementation, which is explicitly not an arm. ZERO MODEL SURFACE ADDED, argued in results/zero-model-delta.txt rather than asserted: no TLA+ action, no TLA+ variable, no new declared effect port, and TLC enumerates 3,678,218 states / 118,573 distinct before and after, the same two figures to the digit. The `content:` and `kind:` manifest keys are optional and every existing manifest generates unchanged. The standing proviso was checked: the two new files codegen writes and the append to case_adapters.toml are all writes under a `specs/` tree, which the existing `spec_tree` port already declares. NO NEW GATE. An unbound port runs, a silent provider runs, a port with no `content:` block runs, and codegen never fails because a mapping is weak. The audit is a print, not an exit code. The only thing that raises is the content assertion itself, which is the oracle firing on a failing case. PREDICTIONS-HP.md was not touched. Reconciled onto epic tip ea45ecf (HP-04 merged at 09b0ced); HP-05's plan entry was re-checked field by field against the amended plan -- goals, contributions, expected effects, local signals, conflict keys, wave, promotion order and predecessor are unchanged by the schedule_revision 2 amendment, which touched only GOAL-simpler-same-behavior. WHERE THE EVIDENCE ACTUALLY IS: `close ticket` consumes specs/tickets/HP-05/ into the append-only record, so every path above now reads specs/.history/hexagonal-prompting-epic/ticket-004-HP-05/ticket/results/. The instruments are sealed beside them under .../ticket/measure/; the 43,128-case corpus is NOT committed and .../ticket/measure/README.md carries the exact commands that regenerate it.

ticket.model_delta_expectation: none expected. OUTCOME: none. No TLA+ action, no TLA+ variable, no new effect port, 1x state space measured rather than assumed (118,573 distinct states before and after). The additions are codegen output and two optional manifest keys on an existing declaration node.
ticket.objective: The one mechanism with a measured, replicated edge. Content-asserting effect providers caught 2 of 6 seeded faults that NOTHING else caught -- the two durable-side ones -- reproduced cell for cell across two rounds and independently replicated by a blind agent on a fresh 16-mutant catalogue at 3 of 3 durable-write mutants under the checking mapping and 0 of 3 under the silent one. That mapping choice is worth 30% of the instrument's entire yield. So make it the DEFAULT rather than a thing an expert configures, and make the alternative loud. Every kill number must name its mapping; a run under a silent mapping must say so unprompted, because its kills are a floor and a green run over-reads. Advisory throughout: nothing refuses, nothing blocks. A report, not a gate.
